scenes.visual: Title card: ONE STRING, ONE SHAPE.

scenes.tts: One changed letter can break a protein. How can a single amino acid matter that much?
scenes.visual: Schematic: a chain of colored beads labelled hemoglobin, one bead pulsing. The question appears as on-screen text.
scenes.narration: One changed letter can break a protein. How can a single amino acid matter that much?

scenes.tts: In sickle cell anemia, one amino acid in hemoglobin is swapped. Glutamate at position six of beta globin becomes valine.
scenes.caption: In sickle cell anemia, one amino acid in hemoglobin is swapped. Glutamate at position 6 of beta-globin becomes valine.
scenes.visual: The pulsing bead flips from a charged red bead labelled Glu6 to a grey oily bead labelled Val6. Label: beta-globin, position 6.
scenes.narration: In sickle cell anemia, one amino acid in hemoglobin is swapped. Glutamate at position 6 of beta-globin becomes valine.

scenes.tts: A charged residue on the surface becomes an oily one.
scenes.visual: Close-up: the bead sits on the outer surface of a rounded hemoglobin blob; its charge sign disappears.
scenes.narration: A charged residue on the surface becomes an oily one.

scenes.tts: Once the hemoglobin releases its oxygen, it sticks together into long fibers.
scenes.visual: Small O2 dots leave the blobs. The blobs line up end to end into long rods. Label: fibers form without oxygen.
scenes.narration: Once the hemoglobin releases its oxygen, it sticks together into long fibers.

scenes.tts: One letter changed the shape, and the shape changed the job.
scenes.visual: Three boxes in a row with arrows: Sequence → Structure → Function. A red cross appears under the last box.
scenes.narration: One letter changed the shape, and the shape changed the job.

scenes.tts: So the shape must be stored somewhere, and stored precisely. But where?
scenes.visual: On-screen text: Where is the shape stored? Three candidate icons: a sequence string, a helper protein, a cell.
scenes.narration: So the shape must be stored somewhere, and stored precisely. But where?

scenes.tts: Start with the chain. Its primary structure is the order of its amino acids, linked end to end by peptide bonds.
scenes.visual: A bead chain stretches across the screen, N-terminus on the left, C-terminus on the right. Label: primary structure = the sequence.
scenes.narration: Start with the chain. Its primary structure is the order of its amino acids, linked end to end by peptide bonds.

scenes.tts: That order is exact, not random. Insulin, for example, is fifty-one residues in one defined order.
scenes.caption: That order is exact, not random. Insulin, for example, is 51 residues in one defined order.
scenes.visual: Counter ticks along the beads: 51 residues, one defined order. Label: insulin.
scenes.narration: That order is exact, not random. Insulin, for example, is 51 residues in one defined order.

scenes.tts: Christian Anfinsen tested where the shape lives. He used ribonuclease, an enzyme with four disulfide bonds.
scenes.visual: Name card: Christian Anfinsen. A compact enzyme blob with four yellow bridges drawn across it, labelled S–S.
scenes.narration: Christian Anfinsen tested where the shape lives. He used ribonuclease, an enzyme with four disulfide bonds.

scenes.tts: Tube one holds the working enzyme. Its activity is full.
scenes.visual: Three test tubes in a row. Tube 1 holds the compact blob; an activity meter beside it reads 100%.
scenes.narration: Tube one holds the working enzyme. Its activity is full.

scenes.tts: In tube two, he added urea and a reducing agent. The reducing agent broke the disulfide bonds. Urea pulled the chain apart.
scenes.visual: Tube 2: labels urea and reducing agent drop in. The yellow bridges snap; the blob loosens into a limp, wandering bead string.
scenes.narration: In tube two, he added urea and a reducing agent. The reducing agent broke the disulfide bonds. Urea pulled the chain apart.

scenes.tts: Activity fell to zero. The enzyme was now a loose, random coil.
scenes.visual: Tube 2 meter falls to 0%. Label: random coil.
scenes.narration: Activity fell to zero. The enzyme was now a loose, random coil.

scenes.tts: In tube three, he washed the chemicals away. No other proteins were there. Just the chain, a buffer, and air.
scenes.visual: Tube 3: the chemical labels drain out. Small text: no helper proteins; buffer; air.
scenes.narration: In tube three, he washed the chemicals away. No other proteins were there. Just the chain, a buffer, and air.

scenes.tts: Here is the test. If the cell's machinery stored the shape, what would tube three show?
scenes.visual: Tube 3 holds the limp coil. On-screen question: If the cell stored the shape, what would tube 3 show?
scenes.narration: Here is the test. If the cell's machinery stored the shape, what would tube three show?

scenes.visual: The question stays on screen; a small countdown ring runs.

scenes.tts: The enzyme refolded on its own, back to full activity. No helper guided it, only its own sequence, in that buffer.
scenes.visual: The coil in tube 3 gathers back into the compact blob. The meter climbs back to 100%.
scenes.narration: The enzyme refolded on its own, back to full activity. No helper guided it, only its own sequence, in that buffer.

scenes.tts: Look at the disulfides. Eight cysteines can pair up in a hundred and five different ways.
scenes.caption: Look at the disulfides. Eight cysteines can pair up in 105 different ways.
scenes.visual: Eight yellow dots on the chain with faint lines flickering between many pairs. On-screen: 8 cysteines, 105 possible pairings.
scenes.narration: Look at the disulfides. Eight cysteines can pair up in 105 different ways.

scenes.tts: Random pairing would get them right less than one time in a hundred. Yet the chain found its correct partners.
scenes.visual: The flickering stops; four bridges settle in their native places and glow. On-screen: random chance < 1%.
scenes.narration: Random pairing would get them right less than one time in a hundred. Yet the chain found its correct partners.

scenes.tts: Anfinsen's conclusion was this. The fold is set by the amino acid sequence, in a given environment.
scenes.visual: Quote card: the native fold is determined by the amino acid sequence, in a given environment. The last phrase is underlined.
scenes.narration: Anfinsen's conclusion was this. The fold is set by the amino acid sequence, in a given environment.

scenes.tts: For most small proteins, the fold is the lowest free energy state the chain can reach.
scenes.visual: A simple bowl-shaped curve; a ball settles at the bottom, labelled native fold, lowest free energy.
scenes.narration: For most small proteins, the fold is the lowest free energy state the chain can reach.

scenes.tts: Free energy here is a trade. The chain gives up freedom. In return, it gains favorable contacts and freer water.
scenes.visual: A balance scale: left pan labelled freedom given up, right pan labelled contacts made, water freed. It tips slightly toward the right pan.
scenes.narration: Free energy here is a trade. The chain gives up freedom. In return, it gains favorable contacts and freer water.

scenes.tts: Keep those words in mind: in a given environment. They will matter later.
scenes.visual: The underlined phrase from the quote card returns and is pinned to the corner of the screen.
scenes.narration: Keep those words in mind: in a given environment. They will matter later.

scenes.tts: Three questions remain. Which shapes are possible? What picks one? And how is it found so fast?
scenes.visual: Three question cards appear side by side: Which shapes are possible? What picks one? How is it found fast?
scenes.narration: Three questions remain. Which shapes are possible? What picks one? And how is it found so fast?

scenes.tts: One rule will answer the first two. Geometry allows the shapes. Water drives the choice. The third question needs one more idea.
scenes.visual: Two words fade in: Geometry allows. Water chooses.
scenes.narration: One rule will answer the first two. Geometry allows the shapes. Water drives the choice. The third question needs one more idea.

scenes.tts: The shape of a protein is written in its sequence.
scenes.visual: End card. LINE: The sequence holds the fold. In the right buffer, the chain refolds with no helper to guide it.
scenes.narration: The shape of a protein is written in its sequence.
